status: registered before any run, smoke tests included
purpose: Close the reviewer questions the first post-review round left open (ICLR 2027 submission 13712): NMa5's oracle for heads and ground truth for embedding atoms, MgDZ's question of what greedy pursuit adds, and MgDZ's comparison with SAE features, which is also 7MWE's setting of a vector no forward pass produced. Follow-up experiments on a different pipeline (five small models, 16,384 states) already measured each of these; their GPT-2 numbers are the priors below. These reruns use the paper's protocol (GPT-2 small, layer 6, 32,768 WikiText-2 states, exp_z2_ci's states, centering, dictionary and ledger).

S1.text: one-shot ranking through the dual frame identifies the largest write at least 0.02 more often than plain one-shot ranking and at least 0.10 more often than OMP (follow-up: 0.80 against 0.77 and 0.64)

S2.text: LASSO identifies the largest write for at least 0.80 of tokens and at least 0.15 more often than OMP (follow-up: 0.85)

S3.text: OMP has the lowest refit FVU on typical states of the four solvers

H1.text: the dominant head by raw write norm has an atom in the OMP support for 0.10 to 0.30 of typical tokens (follow-up: 0.20)

H2.text: when the dominant head is selected, its selected atoms capture a median of under 0.2 of its write energy, raw and centred (follow-up: 0.01 to 0.19)

H3.text: the dominant head (raw) is selected at most three times as often as a random head

H4.text: among selected attention atoms the recovered coefficient has the sign of the true centred coefficient in 0.60 to 0.90 of cases, well short of the 0.998 of identified MLP writes

H5.text: at least half of the selected attention atoms are real by the paper's 5% rule applied to attention coefficients

H6.text: the atom with the largest true attention coefficient is in the support for under 0.30 of typical tokens

E1.text: token-embedding rows are 0.05 to 0.40 of the support on typical tokens (follow-up: 0.09 to 0.36 across models)

E2.text: a selected token row is the current token in under 0.05 of cases (follow-up: 0.00 to 0.027)

E3.text: a selected token row matches an earlier context token less often than a unigram-matched random token does (follow-up: 0.002 to 0.015 against 0.33 to 0.37)

E4.text: the token's own embedding row is in the support for under 0.10 of typical tokens (follow-up: 0.03 from layer 5 on)

E5.text: the token's own position row is in the support for under 0.10 of typical tokens

F1.text: an MLP row is the first atom for at least 0.85 of SAE features (follow-up: 0.93)

F2.text: for random unit directions the first atom is an MLP row in under 0.70 of cases (follow-up: 0.54)

F3.text: sixteen atoms leave a median of 0.40 to 0.56 of an SAE feature unexplained (follow-up: 0.48) and at least 0.15 less than the rotated dictionary leaves (follow-up: 0.72)

F4.text: sixteen atoms leave a median of at least 0.65 of a random direction unexplained (follow-up: 0.72)

F5.text: SAE features are within 0.05 of centred typical states at sixteen atoms (follow-up: 0.48 against 0.47)

honest_overall: I expect the follow-up's picture to reproduce: other solvers identify more than OMP while reconstructing worse; the attention atoms do not track the dominant head and the selected embedding rows are almost never the token's own, so the non-MLP part of the support is not attribution; an SAE feature's first atom is usually an MLP row but a feature is far from a single write. The new measurements with no prior are H3 to H6 and E5, and I am least sure of H4 and H5.
